summary: A Yes vote changes the real property transfer tax from a flat $15 per $1,000 to a tiered rate of $10 to $30 per $1,000 based on sale price, raising about $1 million per year for general city services until ended by voters.

tax.text: The League of Women Voters supports Measure S, which would adjust Albany’s real property transfer tax and raise about $1 million annually for city services.
tax.quote: Measure S — Real Property Transfer Tax : SUPPORT

tax.text: A No vote would reject changing the real property transfer tax structure, which is projected to provide an additional $1 million annually for city services.
tax.quote: It would provide an additional $1 million annually that would support general services
